speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand the cause of your acute diarrhea; can you describe how long you have had these symptoms and what they look like? Additionally, have you noticed any fever, blood in your stool, or recent travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea (likely Clostridioides difficile infection). Given the recent levofloxacin use for pneumonia and the presence of frequent watery diarrhea with abdominal cramping, this is highly suggestive of C. difficile colitis. I recommend immediate testing for C. difficile toxin via stool assay. REQUEST TEST: Stool_C_difficile_toxin.
